meta.title: The Keeper of Gull Rock
meta.instructions: Your first night keeping the Gull Rock light, and a small boat is drifting toward the reef in a storm. Tap a choice to decide what you do. Spare the lamp oil if you can: four endings, two of them happy.

hour.body: if steps < 3 then str(9 + steps) + ' pm' else if steps == 3 then 'Midnight' else str(steps - 3) + ' am'

final_score.body: if verdict == '' then 0 else ending_points() + oil * 50

node.label: Lamp oil
node.value: = if oil == 0 then 'Empty' else str(oil) + (if oil == 1 then ' can' else ' cans')

node.eyebrow: = if verdict == 'good' then 'THE LIGHT HELD' else 'THE LIGHT FAILED'
node.title: = get_or(content_ending_titles, scene, 'Dawn at Gull Rock')
node.line: = 'Ending ' + str(ending_points()) + ' + oil ' + str(oil * 50) + '. One of four endings.'

score.measures: the ending you reached plus 50 for each can of lamp oil left

art.style: A storybook storm at sea: deep slate-blue night, rain streaks, a white-and-red lighthouse with a honey-gold beam, sea-glass cyan highlights.

story_lines: Your first night keeping Gull Rock.
The storm hits at dusk. Then, through
the rain, a small boat's light drifts
toward the reef below the tower.
The great lamp gutters. The oil is
low, and the wind finds every crack.
The boat needs a steady beam to
steer clear of the rocks.
Spray bursts over the jetty steps.
The boat is close now: two people
bailing water. Your rowboat knocks
against its rope below.
The radio crackles. The harbour
answers: 'The lifeboat is out at
the north bank. Forty minutes,
keeper. Hold on.'
The flame leaps high and the beam
sweeps the reef white. Far below,
the little boat turns, slowly, away
from the rocks.
You haul the lens round by hand.
Your arms burn. The beam stutters,
but the boat sees it and tacks
hard to port.
The rowboat bucks like a horse.
You reach them: a fisher and her
nephew, soaked and shaking.
'The reef! We can't see the reef!'
Red flares hiss along the jetty.
The boat swings toward the glow
and scrapes onto the shingle.
Two shapes wave from the deck.
'We're coming,' the harbour says.
You wait by the set. Through the
window, the boat's light slides
closer to the reef each minute.
By dawn the storm has blown out.
The boat rides safe in the cove,
and two tired sailors are drinking
your tea. The light held.
You sit for one breath. When you
look up, the boat's light is gone.
The lifeboat finds them on the
reef at dawn: cold, alive, furious.
You pull them up the steps as the
sea roars behind you. Wrapped in
blankets by the stove, the nephew
asks if he can be a keeper too.
Your rowboat is too small for three.
A wave rolls you all into the surf.
The lifeboat fishes you out at dawn.
Nobody calls you keeper again.
